Threat Modeling Report

Created on 11/18/2026 6:37:11 PM

Threat Model Name: DefectDojo Threat Model (Team 5)

Owner: Team 5

Reviewer:

Contributors: Ray Donner, Alex Bahwawsi, Chandler Crist, Grant Nichter

Description: DefectDojo is an open-source vulnerability management platform. CI/CD pipelines import scanner results through the REST API; security analysts triage findings and record risk acceptances; developers view and remediate findings for the Assets they are authorized on; administrators manage users, access lists and API tokens; and DefectDojo pushes findings to Jira and receives status updates by webhook. The model contains one Level 1 DFD of the container architecture and two Level 2 DFDs that decompose the Django application for the five scenarios from the Security Requirements and Assurance Case assignments.

Assumptions: DefectDojo OSS 3.x deployed with the default Docker Compose stack (nginx, uWSGI, Celery Worker, Celery Beat, initializer, PostgreSQL, Valkey) on a single host. Only nginx publishes ports; all other containers communicate on the internal Docker network without TLS. Users authenticate with local DefectDojo accounts (SSO and MFA are Pro-only in 3.x). Open-source authorization uses Authorized Users lists plus staff / superuser flags (no role separation). Security scanners run inside the CI/CD platform; only the pipeline calls DefectDojo.

External Dependencies: CI/CD platform and security scanners; Atlassian Jira (cloud or server); enterprise corporate network; Docker host operating system.

1. An adversary can tamper critical database securables and deny the action  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:An adversary can tamper critical database securables and deny the action
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Add digital signature to critical database securables. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#securables-db"> https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#securables-db</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://msdn.microsoft.com/library/ms181700
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:In cases where the integrity of a critical database securable has to be verified, digital signatures should be used. Database securables such as a stored procedure, function, assembly, or trigger can be digitally signed. Below is an example of when this can be useful: Let us say an ISV (Independent Software Vendor) has provided support to a software delivered to one of their customers. Before providing support, the ISV would want to ensure that a database securable in the software was not tampered either by mistake or by a malicious attempt. If the securable is digitally signed, the ISV can verify its digital signature and validate its integrity.

2. An adversary may leverage the lack of monitoring systems and trigger anamolous traffic to database  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:An adversary may leverage the lack of intrusion detection and prevention of anomalous database activities and trigger anamolous traffic to database
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Enable Threat detection on Azure SQL database. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#threat-detection"> https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#threat-detection</a>
SDL Phase:Design
Policy:
Documentation:https://azure.microsoft.com/documentation/articles/sql-database-threat-detection-get-started/
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:Threat Detection detects anomalous database activities indicating potential security threats to the database. It provides a new layer of security, which enables customers to detect and respond to potential threats as they occur by providing security alerts on anomalous activities. Users can explore the suspicious events using Azure SQL Database Auditing to determine if they result from an attempt to access, breach or exploit data in the database. Threat Detection makes it simple to address potential threats to the database without the need to be a security expert or manage advanced security monitoring systems

3. An adversary can deny actions on database due to lack of auditing  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: Medium] 

Category:Repudiation
Description:Proper logging of all security events and user actions builds traceability in a system and denies any possible repudiation issues. In the absence of proper auditing and logging controls, it would become impossible to implement any accountability in a system.
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Ensure that login auditing is enabled on SQL Server. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#identify-sensitive-entities"> https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#identify-sensitive-entities</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://msdn.microsoft.com/library/ms175850.aspx
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:Database Server login auditing must be enabled to detect/confirm password guessing attacks. It is important to capture failed login attempts. Capturing both successful and failed login attempts provides additional benefit during forensic investigations

4. An adversary can gain access to sensitive PII or HBI data in PostgreSQL (findings, users, Authorized Users, risk acceptances, API tokens, Jira credentials, audit history)  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Information Disclosure
Description:Additional controls like Transparent Data Encryption, Column Level Encryption, EKM etc. provide additional protection mechanism to high value PII or HBI data.
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Use strong encryption algorithms to encrypt data in the database. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#strong-db"> https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#strong-db</a> Ensure that sensitive data in database columns is encrypted. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtdata#db-encrypted">https://aka.ms/tmtdata#db-encrypted</a> Ensure that database-level encryption (TDE) is enabled. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtdata#tde-enabled">https://aka.ms/tmtdata#tde-enabled</a> Ensure that database backups are encrypted. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtdata#backup">https://aka.ms/tmtdata#backup</a> Use SQL server EKM to protect encryption keys. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#ekm-keys">https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#ekm-keys</a> Use AlwaysEncrypted feature if encryption keys should not be revealed to Database engine. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#keys-engine">https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#keys-engine</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://technet.microsoft.com/library/ms345262(v=sql.130).aspx
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:Encryption algorithms define data transformations that cannot be easily reversed by unauthorized users. SQL Server allows administrators and developers to choose from among several algorithms, including DES, Triple DES, TRIPLE_DES_3KEY, RC2, RC4, 128-bit RC4, DESX, 128-bit AES, 192-bit AES, and 256-bit AES

5. An adversary can gain access to sensitive data by performing SQL injection  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Information Disclosure
Description:SQL injection is an attack in which malicious code is inserted into strings that are later passed to an instance of SQL Server for parsing and execution. The primary form of SQL injection consists of direct insertion of code into user-input variables that are concatenated with SQL commands and executed. A less direct attack injects malicious code into strings that are destined for storage in a table or as metadata. When the stored strings are subsequently concatenated into a dynamic SQL command, the malicious code is executed.
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Ensure that login auditing is enabled on SQL Server. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#identify-sensitive-entities"> https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#identify-sensitive-entities</a> Ensure that least-privileged accounts are used to connect to Database server. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#privileged-server">https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#privileged-server</a> Enable Threat detection on Azure SQL database. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#threat-detection">https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#threat-detection</a> Do not use dynamic queries in stored procedures. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtinputval#stored-proc">https://aka.ms/tmtinputval#stored-proc</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://stackoverflow.com/questions/25558875/how-to-protect-against-asp-net-sql-injections-in-sql-azure
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:A SQL injection attack exploits vulnerabilities in input validation to run arbitrary commands in the database. It can occur when your application uses input to construct dynamic SQL statements to access the database. It can also occur if your code uses stored procedures that are passed strings that contain raw user input. Using the SQL injection attack, the attacker can execute arbitrary commands in the database. All SQL statements (including the SQL statements in stored procedures) must be parameterized. Parameterized SQL statements will accept characters that have special meaning to SQL (like single quote) without problems because they are strongly typed.

Implemented Mitigation(s):

8. An adversary can gain unauthorized access to PostgreSQL (findings, users, Authorized Users, risk acceptances, API tokens, Jira credentials, audit history) due to loose authorization rules  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:Database access should be configured with roles and privilege based on least privilege and need to know principle.
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Ensure that least-privileged accounts are used to connect to Database server. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#privileged-server">https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#privileged-server</a> Implement Row Level Security RLS to prevent tenants from accessing each others data. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#rls-tenants">https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#rls-tenants</a> Sysadmin role should only have valid necessary users . Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#sysadmin-users">https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#sysadmin-users</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://msdn.microsoft.com/library/ms191465
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:Least-privileged accounts should be used to connect to the database. Application login should be restricted in the database and should only execute selected stored procedures. Application's login should have no direct table access.

9. An adversary may gain unauthorized access to PostgreSQL (findings, users, Authorized Users, risk acceptances, API tokens, Jira credentials, audit history) account in a subscription  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:An adversary may gain unauthorized access to PostgreSQL (findings, users, Authorized Users, risk acceptances, API tokens, Jira credentials, audit history) account in a subscription
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Enable Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) to Azure storage account using Azure Resource Manager. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#rbac-azure-manager">https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#rbac-azure-manager</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://azure.microsoft.com/documentation/articles/storage-security-guide/#management-plane-security
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:When you create a new storage account, you select a deployment model of Classic or Azure Resource Manager. The Classic model of creating resources in Azure only allows all-or-nothing access to the subscription, and in turn, the storage account. With the Azure Resource Manager model, you put the storage account in a resource group and control access to the management plane of that specific storage account using Azure Active Directory. For example, you can give specific users the ability to access the storage account keys, while other users can view information about the storage account, but cannot access the storage account keys.

Steps:Threat Detection detects anomalous database activities indicating potential security threats to the database. It provides a new layer of security, which enables customers to detect and respond to potential threats as they occur by providing security alerts on anomalous activities. Users can explore the suspicious events using Azure SQL Database Auditing to determine if they result from an attempt to access, breach or exploit data in the database. Threat Detection makes it simple to address potential threats to the database without the need to be a security expert or manage advanced security monitoring systems

Justification:<no mitigation provided>

Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#strong-db"> https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#strong-db</a> Ensure that sensitive data in database columns is encrypted. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtdata#db-encrypted">https://aka.ms/tmtdata#db-encrypted</a> Ensure that database-level encryption (TDE) is enabled. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtdata#tde-enabled">https://aka.ms/tmtdata#tde-enabled</a> Ensure that database backups are encrypted. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtdata#backup">https://aka.ms/tmtdata#backup</a> Use SQL server EKM to protect encryption keys. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#ekm-keys">https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#ekm-keys</a> Use AlwaysEncrypted feature if encryption keys should not be revealed to Database engine. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#keys-engine">https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#keys-engine</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://technet.microsoft.com/library/ms345262(v=sql.130).aspx
Implemented Mitigation(s):

SQL Server allows administrators and developers to choose from among several algorithms, including DES, Triple DES, TRIPLE_DES_3KEY, RC2, RC4, 128-bit RC4, DESX, 128-bit AES, 192-bit AES, and 256-bit AES

16. An adversary can gain access to sensitive data by performing SQL injection  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Information Disclosure
Description:SQL injection is an attack in which malicious code is inserted into strings that are later passed to an instance of SQL Server for parsing and execution. The primary form of SQL injection consists of direct insertion of code into user-input variables that are concatenated with SQL commands and executed. A less direct attack injects malicious code into strings that are destined for storage in a table or as metadata. When the stored strings are subsequently concatenated into a dynamic SQL command, the malicious code is executed.
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Ensure that login auditing is enabled on SQL Server. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#identify-sensitive-entities"> https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#identify-sensitive-entities</a> Ensure that least-privileged accounts are used to connect to Database server. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#privileged-server">https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#privileged-server</a> Enable Threat detection on Azure SQL database. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#threat-detection">https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#threat-detection</a> Do not use dynamic queries in stored procedures. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtinputval#stored-proc">https://aka.ms/tmtinputval#stored-proc</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://stackoverflow.com/questions/25558875/how-to-protect-against-asp-net-sql-injections-in-sql-azure
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:A SQL injection attack exploits vulnerabilities in input validation to run arbitrary commands in the database. It can occur when your application uses input to construct dynamic SQL statements to access the database. It can also occur if your code uses stored procedures that are passed strings that contain raw user input. Using the SQL injection attack, the attacker can execute arbitrary commands in the database. All SQL statements (including the SQL statements in stored procedures) must be parameterized. Parameterized SQL statements will accept characters that have special meaning to SQL (like single quote) without problems because they are strongly typed.

20. An adversary may gain unauthorized access to PostgreSQL (findings, users, Authorized Users, risk acceptances, API tokens, Jira credentials, audit history) account in a subscription  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:An adversary may gain unauthorized access to PostgreSQL (findings, users, Authorized Users, risk acceptances, API tokens, Jira credentials, audit history) account in a subscription
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Enable Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) to Azure storage account using Azure Resource Manager. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#rbac-azure-manager">https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#rbac-azure-manager</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://azure.microsoft.com/documentation/articles/storage-security-guide/#management-plane-security
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:When you create a new storage account, you select a deployment model of Classic or Azure Resource Manager. The Classic model of creating resources in Azure only allows all-or-nothing access to the subscription, and in turn, the storage account. With the Azure Resource Manager model, you put the storage account in a resource group and control access to the management plane of that specific storage account using Azure Active Directory. For example, you can give specific users the ability to access the storage account keys, while other users can view information about the storage account, but cannot access the storage account keys.

22. An adversary can tamper critical database securables and deny the action  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:An adversary can tamper critical database securables and deny the action
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Add digital signature to critical database securables. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#securables-db"> https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#securables-db</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://msdn.microsoft.com/library/ms181700
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:In cases where the integrity of a critical database securable has to be verified, digital signatures should be used. Database securables such as a stored procedure, function, assembly, or trigger can be digitally signed. Below is an example of when this can be useful: Let us say an ISV (Independent Software Vendor) has provided support to a software delivered to one of their customers. Before providing support, the ISV would want to ensure that a database securable in the software was not tampered either by mistake or by a malicious attempt. If the securable is digitally signed, the ISV can verify its digital signature and validate its integrity.

Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#privileged-server">https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#privileged-server</a> Enable Threat detection on Azure SQL database. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#threat-detection">https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#threat-detection</a> Do not use dynamic queries in stored procedures. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtinputval#stored-proc">https://aka.ms/tmtinputval#stored-proc</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://stackoverflow.com/questions/25558875/how-to-protect-against-asp-net-sql-injections-in-sql-azure
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:A SQL injection attack exploits vulnerabilities in input validation to run arbitrary commands in the database. It can occur when your application uses input to construct dynamic SQL statements to access the database. It can also occur if your code uses stored procedures that are passed strings that contain raw user input. Using the SQL injection attack, the attacker can execute arbitrary commands in the database. All SQL statements (including the SQL statements in stored procedures) must be parameterized. Parameterized SQL statements will accept characters that have special meaning to SQL (like single quote) without problems because they are strongly typed.

30. An adversary may gain unauthorized access to PostgreSQL (findings, users, Authorized Users, risk acceptances, API tokens, Jira credentials, audit history) account in a subscription  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:An adversary may gain unauthorized access to PostgreSQL (findings, users, Authorized Users, risk acceptances, API tokens, Jira credentials, audit history) account in a subscription
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Enable Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) to Azure storage account using Azure Resource Manager. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#rbac-azure-manager">https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#rbac-azure-manager</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://azure.microsoft.com/documentation/articles/storage-security-guide/#management-plane-security
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:When you create a new storage account, you select a deployment model of Classic or Azure Resource Manager. The Classic model of creating resources in Azure only allows all-or-nothing access to the subscription, and in turn, the storage account. With the Azure Resource Manager model, you put the storage account in a resource group and control access to the management plane of that specific storage account using Azure Active Directory. For example, you can give specific users the ability to access the storage account keys, while other users can view information about the storage account, but cannot access the storage account keys.

32. An adversary can tamper critical database securables and deny the action  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:An adversary can tamper critical database securables and deny the action
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Add digital signature to critical database securables. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#securables-db"> https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#securables-db</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://msdn.microsoft.com/library/ms181700
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:In cases where the integrity of a critical database securable has to be verified, digital signatures should be used. Database securables such as a stored procedure, function, assembly, or trigger can be digitally signed. Below is an example of when this can be useful: Let us say an ISV (Independent Software Vendor) has provided support to a software delivered to one of their customers. Before providing support, the ISV would want to ensure that a database securable in the software was not tampered either by mistake or by a malicious attempt. If the securable is digitally signed, the ISV can verify its digital signature and validate its integrity.

33. An adversary may leverage the lack of monitoring systems and trigger anamolous traffic to database  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:An adversary may leverage the lack of intrusion detection and prevention of anomalous database activities and trigger anamolous traffic to database
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Enable Threat detection on Azure SQL database. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#threat-detection"> https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#threat-detection</a>
SDL Phase:Design
Policy:
Documentation:https://azure.microsoft.com/documentation/articles/sql-database-threat-detection-get-started/
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:Threat Detection detects anomalous database activities indicating potential security threats to the database. It provides a new layer of security, which enables customers to detect and respond to potential threats as they occur by providing security alerts on anomalous activities. Users can explore the suspicious events using Azure SQL Database Auditing to determine if they result from an attempt to access, breach or exploit data in the database. Threat Detection makes it simple to address potential threats to the database without the need to be a security expert or manage advanced security monitoring systems

34. An adversary can deny actions on database due to lack of auditing  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: Medium] 

Category:Repudiation
Description:Proper logging of all security events and user actions builds traceability in a system and denies any possible repudiation issues. In the absence of proper auditing and logging controls, it would become impossible to implement any accountability in a system.
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Ensure that login auditing is enabled on SQL Server. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#identify-sensitive-entities"> https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#identify-sensitive-entities</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://msdn.microsoft.com/library/ms175850.aspx
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:Database Server login auditing must be enabled to detect/confirm password guessing attacks. It is important to capture failed login attempts. Capturing both successful and failed login attempts provides additional benefit during forensic investigations

35. An adversary can gain access to sensitive PII or HBI data in Authorized Users Lists  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Information Disclosure
Description:Additional controls like Transparent Data Encryption, Column Level Encryption, EKM etc. provide additional protection mechanism to high value PII or HBI data.
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Use strong encryption algorithms to encrypt data in the database. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#strong-db"> https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#strong-db</a> Ensure that sensitive data in database columns is encrypted. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtdata#db-encrypted">https://aka.ms/tmtdata#db-encrypted</a> Ensure that database-level encryption (TDE) is enabled. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtdata#tde-enabled">https://aka.ms/tmtdata#tde-enabled</a> Ensure that database backups are encrypted. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtdata#backup">https://aka.ms/tmtdata#backup</a> Use SQL server EKM to protect encryption keys. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#ekm-keys">https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#ekm-keys</a> Use AlwaysEncrypted feature if encryption keys should not be revealed to Database engine. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#keys-engine">https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#keys-engine</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://technet.microsoft.com/library/ms345262(v=sql.130).aspx
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:Encryption algorithms define data transformations that cannot be easily reversed by unauthorized users. SQL Server allows administrators and developers to choose from among several algorithms, including DES, Triple DES, TRIPLE_DES_3KEY, RC2, RC4, 128-bit RC4, DESX, 128-bit AES, 192-bit AES, and 256-bit AES

36. An adversary can gain access to sensitive data by performing SQL injection  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Information Disclosure
Description:SQL injection is an attack in which malicious code is inserted into strings that are later passed to an instance of SQL Server for parsing and execution. The primary form of SQL injection consists of direct insertion of code into user-input variables that are concatenated with SQL commands and executed. A less direct attack injects malicious code into strings that are destined for storage in a table or as metadata. When the stored strings are subsequently concatenated into a dynamic SQL command, the malicious code is executed.
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Ensure that login auditing is enabled on SQL Server. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#threat-detection">https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#threat-detection</a> Do not use dynamic queries in stored procedures. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtinputval#stored-proc">https://aka.ms/tmtinputval#stored-proc</a>

Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#sysadmin-users">https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#sysadmin-users</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://msdn.microsoft.com/library/ms191465
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:Least-privileged accounts should be used to connect to the database. Application login should be restricted in the database and should only execute selected stored procedures. Application's login should have no direct table access.

SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://azure.microsoft.com/documentation/articles/storage-security-guide/#management-plane-security
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:When you create a new storage account, you select a deployment model of Classic or Azure Resource Manager. The Classic model of creating resources in Azure only allows all-or-nothing access to the subscription, and in turn, the storage account. With the Azure Resource Manager model, you put the storage account in a resource group and control access to the management plane of that specific storage account using Azure Active Directory. For example, you can give specific users the ability to access the storage account keys, while other users can view information about the storage account, but cannot access the storage account keys.

41. An adversary can tamper critical database securables and deny the action  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:An adversary can tamper critical database securables and deny the action
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Add digital signature to critical database securables. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#securables-db"> https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#securables-db</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://msdn.microsoft.com/library/ms181700
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:In cases where the integrity of a critical database securable has to be verified, digital signatures should be used. Database securables such as a stored procedure, function, assembly, or trigger can be digitally signed. Below is an example of when this can be useful: Let us say an ISV (Independent Software Vendor) has provided support to a software delivered to one of their customers. Before providing support, the ISV would want to ensure that a database securable in the software was not tampered either by mistake or by a malicious attempt. If the securable is digitally signed, the ISV can verify its digital signature and validate its integrity.

42. An adversary may leverage the lack of monitoring systems and trigger anamolous traffic to database  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:An adversary may leverage the lack of intrusion detection and prevention of anomalous database activities and trigger anamolous traffic to database
Justification:<no mitigation provided>

SDL Phase:Design
Policy:
Documentation:https://azure.microsoft.com/documentation/articles/sql-database-threat-detection-get-started/
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:Threat Detection detects anomalous database activities indicating potential security threats to the database. It provides a new layer of security, which enables customers to detect and respond to potential threats as they occur by providing security alerts on anomalous activities. Users can explore the suspicious events using Azure SQL Database Auditing to determine if they result from an attempt to access, breach or exploit data in the database. Threat Detection makes it simple to address potential threats to the database without the need to be a security expert or manage advanced security monitoring systems

43. An adversary can deny actions on database due to lack of auditing  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: Medium] 

Category:Repudiation
Description:Proper logging of all security events and user actions builds traceability in a system and denies any possible repudiation issues. In the absence of proper auditing and logging controls, it would become impossible to implement any accountability in a system.
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Ensure that login auditing is enabled on SQL Server. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#identify-sensitive-entities"> https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#identify-sensitive-entities</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://msdn.microsoft.com/library/ms175850.aspx
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:Database Server login auditing must be enabled to detect/confirm password guessing attacks. It is important to capture failed login attempts. Capturing both successful and failed login attempts provides additional benefit during forensic investigations

44. An adversary can gain access to sensitive PII or HBI data in Findings, Tests, Risk Acceptances  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Information Disclosure
Description:Additional controls like Transparent Data Encryption, Column Level Encryption, EKM etc. provide additional protection mechanism to high value PII or HBI data.
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Use strong encryption algorithms to encrypt data in the database. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#strong-db"> https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#strong-db</a> Ensure that sensitive data in database columns is encrypted. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtdata#db-encrypted">https://aka.ms/tmtdata#db-encrypted</a> Ensure that database-level encryption (TDE) is enabled. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtdata#tde-enabled">https://aka.ms/tmtdata#tde-enabled</a> Ensure that database backups are encrypted. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtdata#backup">https://aka.ms/tmtdata#backup</a> Use SQL server EKM to protect encryption keys. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#ekm-keys">https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#ekm-keys</a> Use AlwaysEncrypted feature if encryption keys should not be revealed to Database engine. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#keys-engine">https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#keys-engine</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://technet.microsoft.com/library/ms345262(v=sql.130).aspx
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:Encryption algorithms define data transformations that cannot be easily reversed by unauthorized users. SQL Server allows administrators and developers to choose from among several algorithms, including DES, Triple DES, TRIPLE_DES_3KEY, RC2, RC4, 128-bit RC4, DESX, 128-bit AES, 192-bit AES, and 256-bit AES

45. An adversary can gain access to sensitive data by performing SQL injection  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Information Disclosure
Description:SQL injection is an attack in which malicious code is inserted into strings that are later passed to an instance of SQL Server for parsing and execution. The primary form of SQL injection consists of direct insertion of code into user-input variables that are concatenated with SQL commands and executed. A less direct attack injects malicious code into strings that are destined for storage in a table or as metadata. When the stored strings are subsequently concatenated into a dynamic SQL command, the malicious code is executed.
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Ensure that login auditing is enabled on SQL Server. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#identify-sensitive-entities"> https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#identify-sensitive-entities</a> Ensure that least-privileged accounts are used to connect to Database server. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#privileged-server">https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#privileged-server</a> Enable Threat detection on Azure SQL database. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#threat-detection">https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#threat-detection</a> Do not use dynamic queries in stored procedures. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtinputval#stored-proc">https://aka.ms/tmtinputval#stored-proc</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://stackoverflow.com/questions/25558875/how-to-protect-against-asp-net-sql-injections-in-sql-azure
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:A SQL injection attack exploits vulnerabilities in input validation to run arbitrary commands in the database. It can occur when your application uses input to construct dynamic SQL statements to access the database. It can also occur if your code uses stored procedures that are passed strings that contain raw user input. Using the SQL injection attack, the attacker can execute arbitrary commands in the database. All SQL statements (including the SQL statements in stored procedures) must be parameterized. Parameterized SQL statements will accept characters that have special meaning to SQL (like single quote) without problems because they are strongly typed.

54. An adversary can gain access to sensitive data by performing SQL injection  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Information Disclosure
Description:SQL injection is an attack in which malicious code is inserted into strings that are later passed to an instance of SQL Server for parsing and execution. The primary form of SQL injection consists of direct insertion of code into user-input variables that are concatenated with SQL commands and executed. A less direct attack injects malicious code into strings that are destined for storage in a table or as metadata. When the stored strings are subsequently concatenated into a dynamic SQL command, the malicious code is executed.
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Ensure that login auditing is enabled on SQL Server. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#identify-sensitive-entities"> https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#identify-sensitive-entities</a> Ensure that least-privileged accounts are used to connect to Database server. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#privileged-server">https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#privileged-server</a> Enable Threat detection on Azure SQL database. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#threat-detection">https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#threat-detection</a> Do not use dynamic queries in stored procedures. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtinputval#stored-proc">https://aka.ms/tmtinputval#stored-proc</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://stackoverflow.com/questions/25558875/how-to-protect-against-asp-net-sql-injections-in-sql-azure
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:A SQL injection attack exploits vulnerabilities in input validation to run arbitrary commands in the database. It can occur when your application uses input to construct dynamic SQL statements to access the database. It can also occur if your code uses stored procedures that are passed strings that contain raw user input. Using the SQL injection attack, the attacker can execute arbitrary commands in the database. All SQL statements (including the SQL statements in stored procedures) must be parameterized. Parameterized SQL statements will accept characters that have special meaning to SQL (like single quote) without problems because they are strongly typed.

58. An adversary may gain unauthorized access to Audit Event Tables (pghistory) account in a subscription  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:An adversary may gain unauthorized access to Audit Event Tables (pghistory) account in a subscription
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Enable Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) to Azure storage account using Azure Resource Manager. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#rbac-azure-manager">https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#rbac-azure-manager</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://azure.microsoft.com/documentation/articles/storage-security-guide/#management-plane-security
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:When you create a new storage account, you select a deployment model of Classic or Azure Resource Manager. The Classic model of creating resources in Azure only allows all-or-nothing access to the subscription, and in turn, the storage account. With the Azure Resource Manager model, you put the storage account in a resource group and control access to the management plane of that specific storage account using Azure Active Directory. For example, you can give specific users the ability to access the storage account keys, while other users can view information about the storage account, but cannot access the storage account keys.

60. An adversary can tamper critical database securables and deny the action  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:An adversary can tamper critical database securables and deny the action
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Add digital signature to critical database securables. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#securables-db"> https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#securables-db</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://msdn.microsoft.com/library/ms181700
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:In cases where the integrity of a critical database securable has to be verified, digital signatures should be used. Database securables such as a stored procedure, function, assembly, or trigger can be digitally signed. Below is an example of when this can be useful: Let us say an ISV (Independent Software Vendor) has provided support to a software delivered to one of their customers. Before providing support, the ISV would want to ensure that a database securable in the software was not tampered either by mistake or by a malicious attempt. If the securable is digitally signed, the ISV can verify its digital signature and validate its integrity.

SDL Phase:Design
Policy:
Documentation:https://azure.microsoft.com/documentation/articles/sql-database-threat-detection-get-started/
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:Threat Detection detects anomalous database activities indicating potential security threats to the database. It provides a new layer of security, which enables customers to detect and respond to potential threats as they occur by providing security alerts on anomalous activities. Users can explore the suspicious events using Azure SQL Database Auditing to determine if they result from an attempt to access, breach or exploit data in the database. Threat Detection makes it simple to address potential threats to the database without the need to be a security expert or manage advanced security monitoring systems

Policy:
Documentation:https://msdn.microsoft.com/library/ms175850.aspx
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:Database Server login auditing must be enabled to detect/confirm password guessing attacks. It is important to capture failed login attempts. Capturing both successful and failed login attempts provides additional benefit during forensic investigations

68. An adversary may gain unauthorized access to Findings, Tests, Risk Acceptances account in a subscription  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:An adversary may gain unauthorized access to Findings, Tests, Risk Acceptances account in a subscription
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Enable Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) to Azure storage account using Azure Resource Manager. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#rbac-azure-manager">https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#rbac-azure-manager</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://azure.microsoft.com/documentation/articles/storage-security-guide/#management-plane-security
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:When you create a new storage account, you select a deployment model of Classic or Azure Resource Manager. The Classic model of creating resources in Azure only allows all-or-nothing access to the subscription, and in turn, the storage account. With the Azure Resource Manager model, you put the storage account in a resource group and control access to the management plane of that specific storage account using Azure Active Directory. For example, you can give specific users the ability to access the storage account keys, while other users can view information about the storage account, but cannot access the storage account keys.

71. An adversary can tamper critical database securables and deny the action  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:An adversary can tamper critical database securables and deny the action
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Add digital signature to critical database securables. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#securables-db"> https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#securables-db</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://msdn.microsoft.com/library/ms181700
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:In cases where the integrity of a critical database securable has to be verified, digital signatures should be used. Database securables such as a stored procedure, function, assembly, or trigger can be digitally signed. Below is an example of when this can be useful: Let us say an ISV (Independent Software Vendor) has provided support to a software delivered to one of their customers. Before providing support, the ISV would want to ensure that a database securable in the software was not tampered either by mistake or by a malicious attempt. If the securable is digitally signed, the ISV can verify its digital signature and validate its integrity.

72. An adversary may leverage the lack of monitoring systems and trigger anamolous traffic to database  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:An adversary may leverage the lack of intrusion detection and prevention of anomalous database activities and trigger anamolous traffic to database
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Enable Threat detection on Azure SQL database. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#threat-detection"> https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#threat-detection</a>
SDL Phase:Design
Policy:
Documentation:https://azure.microsoft.com/documentation/articles/sql-database-threat-detection-get-started/
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:Threat Detection detects anomalous database activities indicating potential security threats to the database. It provides a new layer of security, which enables customers to detect and respond to potential threats as they occur by providing security alerts on anomalous activities. Users can explore the suspicious events using Azure SQL Database Auditing to determine if they result from an attempt to access, breach or exploit data in the database. Threat Detection makes it simple to address potential threats to the database without the need to be a security expert or manage advanced security monitoring systems

73. An adversary can deny actions on database due to lack of auditing  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: Medium] 

Category:Repudiation
Description:Proper logging of all security events and user actions builds traceability in a system and denies any possible repudiation issues. In the absence of proper auditing and logging controls, it would become impossible to implement any accountability in a system.
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Ensure that login auditing is enabled on SQL Server. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#identify-sensitive-entities"> https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#identify-sensitive-entities</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://msdn.microsoft.com/library/ms175850.aspx
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:Database Server login auditing must be enabled to detect/confirm password guessing attacks. It is important to capture failed login attempts. Capturing both successful and failed login attempts provides additional benefit during forensic investigations

74. An adversary can gain access to sensitive PII or HBI data in Findings, Tests, Risk Acceptances  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Information Disclosure
Description:Additional controls like Transparent Data Encryption, Column Level Encryption, EKM etc. provide additional protection mechanism to high value PII or HBI data.
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Use strong encryption algorithms to encrypt data in the database. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#strong-db"> https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#strong-db</a> Ensure that sensitive data in database columns is encrypted. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtdata#db-encrypted">https://aka.ms/tmtdata#db-encrypted</a> Ensure that database-level encryption (TDE) is enabled. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtdata#tde-enabled">https://aka.ms/tmtdata#tde-enabled</a> Ensure that database backups are encrypted. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtdata#backup">https://aka.ms/tmtdata#backup</a> Use SQL server EKM to protect encryption keys. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#ekm-keys">https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#ekm-keys</a> Use AlwaysEncrypted feature if encryption keys should not be revealed to Database engine. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#keys-engine">https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#keys-engine</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://technet.microsoft.com/library/ms345262(v=sql.130).aspx
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:Encryption algorithms define data transformations that cannot be easily reversed by unauthorized users. SQL Server allows administrators and developers to choose from among several algorithms, including DES, Triple DES, TRIPLE_DES_3KEY, RC2, RC4, 128-bit RC4, DESX, 128-bit AES, 192-bit AES, and 256-bit AES

75. An adversary can gain access to sensitive data by performing SQL injection  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Information Disclosure
Description:SQL injection is an attack in which malicious code is inserted into strings that are later passed to an instance of SQL Server for parsing and execution. The primary form of SQL injection consists of direct insertion of code into user-input variables that are concatenated with SQL commands and executed. A less direct attack injects malicious code into strings that are destined for storage in a table or as metadata. When the stored strings are subsequently concatenated into a dynamic SQL command, the malicious code is executed.
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Ensure that login auditing is enabled on SQL Server. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#identify-sensitive-entities"> https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#identify-sensitive-entities</a> Ensure that least-privileged accounts are used to connect to Database server. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#privileged-server">https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#privileged-server</a> Enable Threat detection on Azure SQL database. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#threat-detection">https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#threat-detection</a> Do not use dynamic queries in stored procedures. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtinputval#stored-proc">https://aka.ms/tmtinputval#stored-proc</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://stackoverflow.com/questions/25558875/how-to-protect-against-asp-net-sql-injections-in-sql-azure
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:A SQL injection attack exploits vulnerabilities in input validation to run arbitrary commands in the database. It can occur when your application uses input to construct dynamic SQL statements to access the database. It can also occur if your code uses stored procedures that are passed strings that contain raw user input. Using the SQL injection attack, the attacker can execute arbitrary commands in the database. All SQL statements (including the SQL statements in stored procedures) must be parameterized. Parameterized SQL statements will accept characters that have special meaning to SQL (like single quote) without problems because they are strongly typed.

Possible Mitigation(s):Enable Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) to Azure storage account using Azure Resource Manager. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#rbac-azure-manager">https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#rbac-azure-manager</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://azure.microsoft.com/documentation/articles/storage-security-guide/#management-plane-security
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:When you create a new storage account, you select a deployment model of Classic or Azure Resource Manager. The Classic model of creating resources in Azure only allows all-or-nothing access to the subscription, and in turn, the storage account. With the Azure Resource Manager model, you put the storage account in a resource group and control access to the management plane of that specific storage account using Azure Active Directory. For example, you can give specific users the ability to access the storage account keys, while other users can view information about the storage account, but cannot access the storage account keys.

81. An adversary can tamper critical database securables and deny the action  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:An adversary can tamper critical database securables and deny the action
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Add digital signature to critical database securables. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#securables-db"> https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#securables-db</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://msdn.microsoft.com/library/ms181700
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:In cases where the integrity of a critical database securable has to be verified, digital signatures should be used. Database securables such as a stored procedure, function, assembly, or trigger can be digitally signed. Below is an example of when this can be useful: Let us say an ISV (Independent Software Vendor) has provided support to a software delivered to one of their customers. Before providing support, the ISV would want to ensure that a database securable in the software was not tampered either by mistake or by a malicious attempt. If the securable is digitally signed, the ISV can verify its digital signature and validate its integrity.

82. An adversary may leverage the lack of monitoring systems and trigger anamolous traffic to database  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:An adversary may leverage the lack of intrusion detection and prevention of anomalous database activities and trigger anamolous traffic to database
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Enable Threat detection on Azure SQL database. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#threat-detection"> https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#threat-detection</a>
SDL Phase:Design
Policy:
Documentation:https://azure.microsoft.com/documentation/articles/sql-database-threat-detection-get-started/
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:Threat Detection detects anomalous database activities indicating potential security threats to the database. It provides a new layer of security, which enables customers to detect and respond to potential threats as they occur by providing security alerts on anomalous activities. Users can explore the suspicious events using Azure SQL Database Auditing to determine if they result from an attempt to access, breach or exploit data in the database. Threat Detection makes it simple to address potential threats to the database without the need to be a security expert or manage advanced security monitoring systems

83. An adversary can deny actions on database due to lack of auditing  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: Medium] 

Category:Repudiation
Description:Proper logging of all security events and user actions builds traceability in a system and denies any possible repudiation issues. In the absence of proper auditing and logging controls, it would become impossible to implement any accountability in a system.
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Ensure that login auditing is enabled on SQL Server. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#identify-sensitive-entities"> https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#identify-sensitive-entities</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://msdn.microsoft.com/library/ms175850.aspx
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:Database Server login auditing must be enabled to detect/confirm password guessing attacks. It is important to capture failed login attempts. Capturing both successful and failed login attempts provides additional benefit during forensic investigations

84. An adversary can gain access to sensitive PII or HBI data in Users and API Tokens  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Information Disclosure
Description:Additional controls like Transparent Data Encryption, Column Level Encryption, EKM etc. provide additional protection mechanism to high value PII or HBI data.
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Use strong encryption algorithms to encrypt data in the database. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#strong-db"> https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#strong-db</a> Ensure that sensitive data in database columns is encrypted. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtdata#db-encrypted">https://aka.ms/tmtdata#db-encrypted</a> Ensure that database-level encryption (TDE) is enabled. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtdata#tde-enabled">https://aka.ms/tmtdata#tde-enabled</a> Ensure that database backups are encrypted. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtdata#backup">https://aka.ms/tmtdata#backup</a> Use SQL server EKM to protect encryption keys. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#ekm-keys">https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#ekm-keys</a> Use AlwaysEncrypted feature if encryption keys should not be revealed to Database engine. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#keys-engine">https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#keys-engine</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://technet.microsoft.com/library/ms345262(v=sql.130).aspx
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:Encryption algorithms define data transformations that cannot be easily reversed by unauthorized users. SQL Server allows administrators and developers to choose from among several algorithms, including DES, Triple DES, TRIPLE_DES_3KEY, RC2, RC4, 128-bit RC4, DESX, 128-bit AES, 192-bit AES, and 256-bit AES

85. An adversary can gain access to sensitive data by performing SQL injection  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Information Disclosure
Description:SQL injection is an attack in which malicious code is inserted into strings that are later passed to an instance of SQL Server for parsing and execution. The primary form of SQL injection consists of direct insertion of code into user-input variables that are concatenated with SQL commands and executed. A less direct attack injects malicious code into strings that are destined for storage in a table or as metadata. When the stored strings are subsequently concatenated into a dynamic SQL command, the malicious code is executed.
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Ensure that login auditing is enabled on SQL Server. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#identify-sensitive-entities"> https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#identify-sensitive-entities</a> Ensure that least-privileged accounts are used to connect to Database server. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#privileged-server">https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#privileged-server</a> Enable Threat detection on Azure SQL database. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#threat-detection">https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#threat-detection</a> Do not use dynamic queries in stored procedures. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtinputval#stored-proc">https://aka.ms/tmtinputval#stored-proc</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://stackoverflow.com/questions/25558875/how-to-protect-against-asp-net-sql-injections-in-sql-azure
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:A SQL injection attack exploits vulnerabilities in input validation to run arbitrary commands in the database. It can occur when your application uses input to construct dynamic SQL statements to access the database. It can also occur if your code uses stored procedures that are passed strings that contain raw user input. Using the SQL injection attack, the attacker can execute arbitrary commands in the database. All SQL statements (including the SQL statements in stored procedures) must be parameterized. Parameterized SQL statements will accept characters that have special meaning to SQL (like single quote) without problems because they are strongly typed.

Category:Information Disclosure
Description:Additional controls like Transparent Data Encryption, Column Level Encryption, EKM etc. provide additional protection mechanism to high value PII or HBI data.
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Use strong encryption algorithms to encrypt data in the database. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#strong-db"> https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#strong-db</a> Ensure that sensitive data in database columns is encrypted. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtdata#db-encrypted">https://aka.ms/tmtdata#db-encrypted</a> Ensure that database-level encryption (TDE) is enabled. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtdata#tde-enabled">https://aka.ms/tmtdata#tde-enabled</a> Ensure that database backups are encrypted. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtdata#backup">https://aka.ms/tmtdata#backup</a> Use SQL server EKM to protect encryption keys. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#ekm-keys">https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#ekm-keys</a> Use AlwaysEncrypted feature if encryption keys should not be revealed to Database engine. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#keys-engine">https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#keys-engine</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://technet.microsoft.com/library/ms345262(v=sql.130).aspx
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:Encryption algorithms define data transformations that cannot be easily reversed by unauthorized users. SQL Server allows administrators and developers to choose from among several algorithms, including DES, Triple DES, TRIPLE_DES_3KEY, RC2, RC4, 128-bit RC4, DESX, 128-bit AES, 192-bit AES, and 256-bit AES

94. An adversary can gain access to sensitive data by performing SQL injection  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Information Disclosure
Description:SQL injection is an attack in which malicious code is inserted into strings that are later passed to an instance of SQL Server for parsing and execution. The primary form of SQL injection consists of direct insertion of code into user-input variables that are concatenated with SQL commands and executed. A less direct attack injects malicious code into strings that are destined for storage in a table or as metadata. When the stored strings are subsequently concatenated into a dynamic SQL command, the malicious code is executed.
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Ensure that login auditing is enabled on SQL Server. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#identify-sensitive-entities"> https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#identify-sensitive-entities</a> Ensure that least-privileged accounts are used to connect to Database server. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#privileged-server">https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#privileged-server</a> Enable Threat detection on Azure SQL database. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#threat-detection">https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#threat-detection</a> Do not use dynamic queries in stored procedures. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtinputval#stored-proc">https://aka.ms/tmtinputval#stored-proc</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://stackoverflow.com/questions/25558875/how-to-protect-against-asp-net-sql-injections-in-sql-azure
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:A SQL injection attack exploits vulnerabilities in input validation to run arbitrary commands in the database. It can occur when your application uses input to construct dynamic SQL statements to access the database. It can also occur if your code uses stored procedures that are passed strings that contain raw user input. Using the SQL injection attack, the attacker can execute arbitrary commands in the database. All SQL statements (including the SQL statements in stored procedures) must be parameterized. Parameterized SQL statements will accept characters that have special meaning to SQL (like single quote) without problems because they are strongly typed.

98. An adversary may gain unauthorized access to Audit Event Tables (pghistory) account in a subscription  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:An adversary may gain unauthorized access to Audit Event Tables (pghistory) account in a subscription
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Enable Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) to Azure storage account using Azure Resource Manager. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#rbac-azure-manager">https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#rbac-azure-manager</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://azure.microsoft.com/documentation/articles/storage-security-guide/#management-plane-security
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:When you create a new storage account, you select a deployment model of Classic or Azure Resource Manager. The Classic model of creating resources in Azure only allows all-or-nothing access to the subscription, and in turn, the storage account. With the Azure Resource Manager model, you put the storage account in a resource group and control access to the management plane of that specific storage account using Azure Active Directory. For example, you can give specific users the ability to access the storage account keys, while other users can view information about the storage account, but cannot access the storage account keys.

99. An adversary can tamper critical database securables and deny the action  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:An adversary can tamper critical database securables and deny the action
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Add digital signature to critical database securables. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#securables-db"> https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#securables-db</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://msdn.microsoft.com/library/ms181700
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:In cases where the integrity of a critical database securable has to be verified, digital signatures should be used. Database securables such as a stored procedure, function, assembly, or trigger can be digitally signed. Below is an example of when this can be useful: Let us say an ISV (Independent Software Vendor) has provided support to a software delivered to one of their customers. Before providing support, the ISV would want to ensure that a database securable in the software was not tampered either by mistake or by a malicious attempt. If the securable is digitally signed, the ISV can verify its digital signature and validate its integrity.

SDL Phase:Design
Policy:
Documentation:https://azure.microsoft.com/documentation/articles/sql-database-threat-detection-get-started/
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:Threat Detection detects anomalous database activities indicating potential security threats to the database. It provides a new layer of security, which enables customers to detect and respond to potential threats as they occur by providing security alerts on anomalous activities. Users can explore the suspicious events using Azure SQL Database Auditing to determine if they result from an attempt to access, breach or exploit data in the database. Threat Detection makes it simple to address potential threats to the database without the need to be a security expert or manage advanced security monitoring systems

Policy:
Documentation:https://msdn.microsoft.com/library/ms175850.aspx
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:Database Server login auditing must be enabled to detect/confirm password guessing attacks. It is important to capture failed login attempts. Capturing both successful and failed login attempts provides additional benefit during forensic investigations

107. An adversary may gain unauthorized access to Jira Instance Record (password stored unencrypted) account in a subscription  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:An adversary may gain unauthorized access to Jira Instance Record (password stored unencrypted) account in a subscription
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Enable Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) to Azure storage account using Azure Resource Manager. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#rbac-azure-manager">https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#rbac-azure-manager</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://azure.microsoft.com/documentation/articles/storage-security-guide/#management-plane-security
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:When you create a new storage account, you select a deployment model of Classic or Azure Resource Manager. The Classic model of creating resources in Azure only allows all-or-nothing access to the subscription, and in turn, the storage account. With the Azure Resource Manager model, you put the storage account in a resource group and control access to the management plane of that specific storage account using Azure Active Directory. For example, you can give specific users the ability to access the storage account keys, while other users can view information about the storage account, but cannot access the storage account keys.

108. An adversary can tamper critical database securables and deny the action  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:An adversary can tamper critical database securables and deny the action
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Add digital signature to critical database securables. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#securables-db"> https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#securables-db</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://msdn.microsoft.com/library/ms181700
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:In cases where the integrity of a critical database securable has to be verified, digital signatures should be used. Database securables such as a stored procedure, function, assembly, or trigger can be digitally signed. Below is an example of when this can be useful: Let us say an ISV (Independent Software Vendor) has provided support to a software delivered to one of their customers. Before providing support, the ISV would want to ensure that a database securable in the software was not tampered either by mistake or by a malicious attempt. If the securable is digitally signed, the ISV can verify its digital signature and validate its integrity.

109. An adversary may leverage the lack of monitoring systems and trigger anamolous traffic to database  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:An adversary may leverage the lack of intrusion detection and prevention of anomalous database activities and trigger anamolous traffic to database
Justification:<no mitigation provided>

SDL Phase:Design
Policy:
Documentation:https://azure.microsoft.com/documentation/articles/sql-database-threat-detection-get-started/
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:Threat Detection detects anomalous database activities indicating potential security threats to the database. It provides a new layer of security, which enables customers to detect and respond to potential threats as they occur by providing security alerts on anomalous activities. Users can explore the suspicious events using Azure SQL Database Auditing to determine if they result from an attempt to access, breach or exploit data in the database. Threat Detection makes it simple to address potential threats to the database without the need to be a security expert or manage advanced security monitoring systems

110. An adversary can deny actions on database due to lack of auditing  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: Medium] 

Category:Repudiation
Description:Proper logging of all security events and user actions builds traceability in a system and denies any possible repudiation issues. In the absence of proper auditing and logging controls, it would become impossible to implement any accountability in a system.
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Ensure that login auditing is enabled on SQL Server. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#identify-sensitive-entities"> https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#identify-sensitive-entities</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://msdn.microsoft.com/library/ms175850.aspx
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:Database Server login auditing must be enabled to detect/confirm password guessing attacks. It is important to capture failed login attempts. Capturing both successful and failed login attempts provides additional benefit during forensic investigations

111. An adversary can gain access to sensitive PII or HBI data in System Settings (Jira enabled, webhook secret)  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Information Disclosure
Description:Additional controls like Transparent Data Encryption, Column Level Encryption, EKM etc. provide additional protection mechanism to high value PII or HBI data.
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Use strong encryption algorithms to encrypt data in the database. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#strong-db"> https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#strong-db</a> Ensure that sensitive data in database columns is encrypted. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtdata#db-encrypted">https://aka.ms/tmtdata#db-encrypted</a> Ensure that database-level encryption (TDE) is enabled. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtdata#tde-enabled">https://aka.ms/tmtdata#tde-enabled</a> Ensure that database backups are encrypted. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtdata#backup">https://aka.ms/tmtdata#backup</a> Use SQL server EKM to protect encryption keys. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#ekm-keys">https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#ekm-keys</a> Use AlwaysEncrypted feature if encryption keys should not be revealed to Database engine. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#keys-engine">https://aka.ms/tmtcrypto#keys-engine</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://technet.microsoft.com/library/ms345262(v=sql.130).aspx
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:Encryption algorithms define data transformations that cannot be easily reversed by unauthorized users. SQL Server allows administrators and developers to choose from among several algorithms, including DES, Triple DES, TRIPLE_DES_3KEY, RC2, RC4, 128-bit RC4, DESX, 128-bit AES, 192-bit AES, and 256-bit AES

112. An adversary can gain access to sensitive data by performing SQL injection  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Information Disclosure
Description:SQL injection is an attack in which malicious code is inserted into strings that are later passed to an instance of SQL Server for parsing and execution. The primary form of SQL injection consists of direct insertion of code into user-input variables that are concatenated with SQL commands and executed. A less direct attack injects malicious code into strings that are destined for storage in a table or as metadata. When the stored strings are subsequently concatenated into a dynamic SQL command, the malicious code is executed.
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Ensure that login auditing is enabled on SQL Server. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#identify-sensitive-entities"> https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#identify-sensitive-entities</a> Ensure that least-privileged accounts are used to connect to Database server. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#privileged-server">https://aka.ms/tmtauthz#privileged-server</a> Enable Threat detection on Azure SQL database. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#threat-detection">https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#threat-detection</a> Do not use dynamic queries in stored procedures. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtinputval#stored-proc">https://aka.ms/tmtinputval#stored-proc</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://stackoverflow.com/questions/25558875/how-to-protect-against-asp-net-sql-injections-in-sql-azure
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:A SQL injection attack exploits vulnerabilities in input validation to run arbitrary commands in the database. It can occur when your application uses input to construct dynamic SQL statements to access the database. It can also occur if your code uses stored procedures that are passed strings that contain raw user input. Using the SQL injection attack, the attacker can execute arbitrary commands in the database. All SQL statements (including the SQL statements in stored procedures) must be parameterized. Parameterized SQL statements will accept characters that have special meaning to SQL (like single quote) without problems because they are strongly typed.

119. An adversary may leverage the lack of monitoring systems and trigger anamolous traffic to database  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Tampering
Description:An adversary may leverage the lack of intrusion detection and prevention of anomalous database activities and trigger anamolous traffic to database
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Enable Threat detection on Azure SQL database. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#threat-detection"> https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#threat-detection</a>
SDL Phase:Design
Policy:
Documentation:https://azure.microsoft.com/documentation/articles/sql-database-threat-detection-get-started/
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:Threat Detection detects anomalous database activities indicating potential security threats to the database. It provides a new layer of security, which enables customers to detect and respond to potential threats as they occur by providing security alerts on anomalous activities. Users can explore the suspicious events using Azure SQL Database Auditing to determine if they result from an attempt to access, breach or exploit data in the database. Threat Detection makes it simple to address potential threats to the database without the need to be a security expert or manage advanced security monitoring systems

120. An adversary can deny actions on database due to lack of auditing  [State: Not Started]  [Priority: Medium] 

Category:Repudiation
Description:Proper logging of all security events and user actions builds traceability in a system and denies any possible repudiation issues. In the absence of proper auditing and logging controls, it would become impossible to implement any accountability in a system.
Justification:<no mitigation provided>
Possible Mitigation(s):Ensure that login auditing is enabled on SQL Server. Refer: <a href="https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#identify-sensitive-entities"> https://aka.ms/tmtauditlog#identify-sensitive-entities</a>
SDL Phase:Implementation
Policy:
Documentation:https://msdn.microsoft.com/library/ms175850.aspx
Implemented Mitigation(s):
Steps:Database Server login auditing must be enabled to detect/confirm password guessing attacks. It is important to capture failed login attempts. Capturing both successful and failed login attempts provides additional benefit during forensic investigations
